title: A git process outlives its test and breaks TempDir cleanup
description:
CI failed on PR #26 with no assertion failing:

    --- FAIL: TestAChangedGateCommandIsNotEvidenceForTheGateDeclaredNow (24.37s)
        testing.go:1267: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat
        /tmp/TestAChangedGateCommand.../002/.git/objects: directory not empty

The test passed. What failed is Go's t.TempDir cleanup: RemoveAll walked .git/objects and something WROTE INTO IT while the walk was running, so the directory was not empty when unlinkat reached it. That is a git process still alive after the test that started it returned.

Same family as the two we already fixed: git auto-maintenance repacking and deleting object subdirectories mid-write, which gitbin.NoAutoMaintenance stops, and the pre-rmc teardown that killed scraped pids. Different in that this one is about a child outliving its TEST rather than corrupting a repository.

Candidates, in order of likelihood:
- a git subprocess the test started and did not wait for, most likely a fetch or a push to a fixture remote;
- auto-maintenance on a path that does not carry gitbin.NoAutoMaintenance - the flags are added by repoGit.run, so any git invocation NOT going through it is exposed (this is the same gap I wrongly suspected for m78, worth actually checking here);
- a worktree or gate process that outlives the reconciler in the fixture.

Not caused by the change it failed on: PR #26 touches internal/factory only and never internal/reconcile.

Do not fix this by retrying the cleanup or by t.TempDir-ing somewhere that does not get cleaned. Find the process and make the test wait for it - a test that leaves a child running is a test that will eventually corrupt the next one's fixture.
notes: 2026-09-21 19:13 - Confirmed INTERMITTENT: re-ran the same commit on PR #26 and the go job went green. So it is a race, not a deterministic break - which is consistent with a git child outliving its test rather than with anything in the change it failed on.
acceptance_criteria: The reconcile suite leaves no git process running after any test returns, proven by a check that fails when one does
